title: Weight decomposition of coherent modules on a trivially acted torus scheme
statement:
Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field], $T\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$ a split torus of rank $r\geq0$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sc-gm-ga], and $Z$ a Noetherian $F$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], where Noetherian means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Give $Z$ the trivial $T$-action. Put $X=\operatorname{Hom}(T,\mathbf G_m)$ and $R=\mathbf Z[X]$, with basis $e^\chi$ and multiplication $e^\chi e^\psi=e^{\chi+\psi}$. A $T$-linearized coherent module is a coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module [pqf-def-coherent] with an isomorphism $a^*\mathcal M\simeq\operatorname{pr}_2^*\mathcal M$ on $T\times_F Z$, satisfying identity and cocycle, with geometric fibre action from $z$ to $tz$. Every such $\mathcal M$ has a unique finite direct-sum decomposition $\mathcal M=\bigoplus_{\chi\in X}\mathcal M_\chi$, in which $T$ acts on $\mathcal M_\chi$ by the character $\chi$ on every geometric fibre and after every algebra extension. The summands are coherent; taking a summand is exact, commutes with restriction and field extension, and carries locally finite free modules to locally finite free modules. Tensor products add weights. For a locally finite free module $E=\bigoplus E_\chi$, forgetting the character on each $E_\chi$, the tensor action of its exterior powers is encoded by the finite polynomial
$$\sum_{q\geq0}[\bigwedge^q E]t^q=\prod_\chi\left(\sum_{j\geq0}[\bigwedge^j E_\chi]e^{j\chi}t^j\right).$$
Here classes act by tensoring coherent modules. In particular there is an $R$-linear isomorphism
$$G_0(Z)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}R\xrightarrow{\sim}G_0^T(Z),\qquad [\mathcal A]\otimes e^\chi\longmapsto[\mathcal A\text{ with character }\chi].$$
Both groups are generated by isomorphism classes of (respectively ordinary and linearized) coherent modules with short exact sequence relations. The ring $R$ acts by character twists. For any finite set of locally finite free modules on $Z$, there is a finite partition of $Z$ into open and closed subschemes on each of which all their ranks are constant; the coherent groups, tensor operators and the displayed isomorphism decompose as the corresponding finite direct sums. A locally finite free weight summand is zero if its fibre is zero at every closed point of $Z$.

source.place: Tags 0EKJ (example-Gm-on-affine), 0EKK (lemma-complete-reducibility-Gm), 0EKL (lemma-Gm-equivariant-module). Agent-formulated finite-rank torus and coherent gluing consequences; Milne Theorem 12.12, printed pp.234--235, gives the coefficient projections. proof.text: By [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality] and [def-sfb-diagonalizable-group], identify $T=D_F(X)$ and $F[T]=F[X]$ with $\Delta(e^\chi)=e^\chi\otimes e^\chi$. On an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ write $M=\mathcal M(U)$. The affine equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] and pullback sections [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] turn the linearization into the datum of [lem-sfb-hopf-coaction-linearization], with trivial algebra coaction $a\mapsto a\otimes1$. Thus its module coaction is $A$-linear. Fix the sign convention as follows: the cited node uses arrows from $x\cdot t$ to $x$, whereas the item labels the action from $x$ to $tx$. Therefore write its coaction as $\theta(m)=\sum_\chi p_\chi(m)\otimes e^{-\chi}$; the inverse linearization, evaluated at $t$, acts by $\chi(t)$ on a vector with $\theta(m)=m\otimes e^{-\chi}$. This gives exactly the forward fibre convention in the item.

source.place: Tag 03LF (definition-equivariant-module); affine coaction translation, with inverse for the forward fibre action. Milne 12.9 and 12.12, pp.233--235.

proof.text: Compare coefficients in the two coaction identities of [lem-sfb-hopf-coaction-linearization]. Counit gives $m=\sum_\chi p_\chi(m)$, a finite sum for each $m$. Coassociativity gives $p_\psi p_\chi=0$ for $\psi\ne\chi$ and $p_\chi^2=p_\chi$, since the coefficient of $e^{-\psi}\otimes e^{-\chi}$ is respectively $p_\psi p_\chi(m)$ and $\delta_{\psi,\chi}p_\chi(m)$. Set $M_\chi=\operatorname{im}p_\chi=\{m:\theta(m)=m\otimes e^{-\chi}\}$. The sum map $\bigoplus_\chi M_\chi\to M$ has inverse $m\mapsto(p_\chi(m))_\chi$: composing either way uses these identities. Any decomposition with the specified action after every algebra extension has these same summands, by evaluating at the universal torus point in $A[X]$ and comparing coefficients. This proves uniqueness scheme-theoretically, including nilpotent bases, rather than testing only rational points.

source.place: Tags 0EKK (lemma-complete-reducibility-Gm), 0EKL (lemma-Gm-equivariant-module), coefficient calculation for the module; Milne Theorem 12.12, p.235.

proof.text: The coherent module is quasi-coherent of finite type by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]; hence $M$ is finite over $A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine]. Choose generators $m_1,\ldots,m_s$. The union $S_U$ of their coefficient supports is finite. Because every $p_\chi$ is $A$-linear, it vanishes on all generators, hence on $M$, if $\chi\notin S_U$. Moreover $M_\chi$ is generated by the $p_\chi(m_i)$. For $V\subset U$ affine, [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-affine-section-base-change] identifies restriction with scalar extension; the coaction and its projections become $p_\chi\otimes1$. The associated modules $\widetilde{M_\chi}$ therefore agree on all affine subopens of overlaps. They glue to submodules $\mathcal M_\chi\subset\mathcal M$ (alternatively apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-object-open-descent] to these canonical overlap identifications). Coherence follows from [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] and the displayed finite generators. Quasi-compactness of $Z$ gives a finite affine cover, so $\bigcup_U S_U$ is finite. The local direct-sum identities are consequently a global finite direct-sum identity.

source.place: Tag 0EKL (lemma-Gm-equivariant-module); finite generation and canonical affine gluing, using Tags 01XZ, 01PB, 01LN, 00AL and 00AM.

proof.text: An equivariant map commutes with coactions by [lem-sfb-hopf-coaction-linearization], hence with all coefficient projections. In an equivariant short exact sequence, a local lift of a section of the quotient of weight $\chi$ can be replaced by its $p_\chi$-projection; this remains a lift and has weight $\chi$. The same projection identities identify the kernel with the $\chi$-part of the original kernel. Thus taking weights is exact as a functor on coherent sheaves. For any $A$-algebra $B$, tensor the split identity $M=\bigoplus M_\chi$ with $B$. Its projections are $1\otimes p_\chi$, so coefficient comparison shows $(B\otimes_A M)_\chi=B\otimes_A M_\chi$, without a flatness hypothesis. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections], this proves the required field-extension compatibility and, together with step 3, restriction compatibility. Coherent kernels and cokernels remain coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth].

source.place: Tag 0EKL (lemma-Gm-equivariant-module), functorial coefficient projections; affine base change and local lifting argument.

proof.text: If $\mathcal M$ is finite locally free, choose an affine trivializing open $U$ with $M=A^n$. Each $M_\chi$ is a direct summand of $A^n$, with complementary summand $\ker p_\chi$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-standard-free-cover], it is free of finite rank on a finite standard-open cover of $U$. Sheafifying the split identity by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] gives the corresponding local trivializations of $\mathcal M_\chi$, using [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-free-module]. Thus every weight summand is finite locally free, with rank allowed to vary.

source.place: Tag 00NX (lemma-finite-projective), direct summands of finite free modules are finite locally free; Tags 01HV and 01I7 for the associated free sheaf.

proof.text: The tensor coaction formula in [lem-sfb-hopf-coaction-linearization] sends $m_\chi\otimes n_\psi$ to $(m_\chi\otimes n_\psi)\otimes e^{-(\chi+\psi)}$. Distributing the finite direct sums shows that the weight $\eta$ part is $\bigoplus_{\chi+\psi=\eta}\mathcal M_\chi\otimes\mathcal N_\psi$, using the affine tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-tensor-product-affine-sections]. If $E$ is finite locally free and $\mathcal A$ is coherent, on each trivializing open $E\otimes\mathcal A$ is a finite direct sum of $\mathcal A$ and tensoring a short exact sequence is its finite direct sum, hence exact. Coherence is local and finite sums are coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth]. Therefore these tensor operations induce operators on the groups with the stated short exact sequence relations.

source.place: Tag 03LF (definition-equivariant-module), tensor coaction; Tags 01I8 and 01Y0, affine tensor and coherent finite sums.

proof.text: Order the finite weight support of $E$. Concatenating wedges in that order defines, for each $q$, a morphism from $\bigoplus_{\sum j_\chi=q}\bigotimes_\chi\bigwedge^{j_\chi}E_\chi$ to $\bigwedge^q E$. It is well-defined by the alternating multilinear relations in [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra]. Locally choose bases for the finitely many $E_\chi$. By [lem-weil-pbc-exterior-power-free-basis], this map sends the tensor products of increasing basis wedges bijectively to the increasing wedges of the concatenated basis of $E$: a subset of that basis is uniquely a subset in each weight block. Hence it is an isomorphism. The maps glue because concatenation uses only the inclusions of the summands, and commutes with restriction by its pure-wedge formula. Step 6 shows its summand has character $\sum j_\chi\chi$. Forgetting each summand's character gives exactly the displayed product identity of tensor operators. A finite trivializing cover bounds all ranks and hence all degrees; wedges above the corresponding ranks vanish by the same cited basis theorem. The argument also covers $q=0$ and empty weight support.

source.place: Tag 00DM (section-tensor-algebra), alternating relations and basis of exterior powers; direct-sum formula proved by partitioning a basis subset.

proof.text: Send $[\mathcal A]\otimes e^\chi$ to the class of $\mathcal A$ with scalar character $\chi$. Character twists preserve short exact sequences, so the presentation of $G_0(Z)$ and the bilinearity relations of the tensor product give a homomorphism $\Phi$. Define $\Psi([\mathcal M])=\sum_\chi[\mathcal M_\chi]\otimes e^\chi$, forgetting the character in each bracket. Step 3 makes the sum finite, and step 4 makes it additive on every short exact sequence, so it descends to $G_0^T(Z)$. Uniqueness in step 2 gives $\Psi\Phi([\mathcal A]\otimes e^\chi)=[\mathcal A]\otimes e^\chi$. The finite direct-sum decomposition, with the relations for its split short exact sequences, gives $\Phi\Psi([\mathcal M])=[\mathcal M]$. Twisting by $\eta$ replaces $\mathcal M_\chi$ by the same ordinary module in weight $\chi+\eta$, so both maps are $R$-linear. Tensor compatibility is step 6.

source.place: Agent assembly from the coefficient decomposition and exactness proved in steps 2--6, using the group presentations in the statement.

proof.text: For each of the finitely many finite locally free modules in question, its rank is constant on every trivializing open, since the fibre of $\mathcal O^n$ over a residue field has dimension $n$. Each rank fibre is open and its complement is the union of the other rank fibres, hence also open. Quasi-compactness gives a finite trivializing subcover, so only finitely many ranks occur. Intersect these finite clopen partitions for the finitely many modules. On the resulting pieces every rank is constant. For a finite disjoint clopen cover, the sheaf condition identifies sections on any open with the product of sections on its intersections with the pieces. Thus restriction and extension by zero are inverse between modules on $Z$ and families of modules on the pieces. Coherence, linearization, exact sequences and tensor are all componentwise, by their local definitions; for coherence use [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. The finite products here are finite direct sums, so the same presentations give direct-sum decompositions of both coherent groups. The maps $\Phi$ and $\Psi$ are componentwise because the coefficient projections commute with restriction, proving the partition compatibility.

source.place: Tag 01C6 (definition-locally-free); finite clopen partition argument from local bases and quasi-compactness; Tag 01XZ for local coherence.

proof.text: For a finite locally free weight summand $P$, its nonzero-rank locus $C$ is clopen by step 9. The underlying space of $Z$ is Kolmogorov: by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober], the irreducible closed set $\overline{\{x\}}$ has a unique generic point, so two points with the same closure coincide. Apply [lem-sc-quasi-compact-kolmogorov-closed-point] to the closed subset $C$ of the quasi-compact scheme $Z$. If $C$ were nonempty, it would contain a point closed in $Z$. At that point the fibre of $P$ would have positive dimension, contradicting the hypothesis. Hence $C$ is empty; every local trivialization has rank zero and $P=0$. This argument needs no Jacobson or finite-type hypothesis on $Z$.

source.place: Tag 005E (lemma-quasi-compact-closed-point), applied to the clopen nonzero-rank locus; Tag 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober).

Step 2: coefficient comparison matches the 0EKK proof; uniqueness uses the universal point, so it is valid over nilpotent bases and finite fields. Step 3: p_chi are A-linear; restriction compatibility uses the nested-affine section base change (no affine overlaps assumed, E1 OK); finite support follows from quasi-compactness. Steps 4-7: exactness by projecting local lifts; arbitrary base change without flatness; summands locally free via the standard free cover; weights add; the exterior concatenation map is an isomorphism via the free-basis node over any ring. Steps 8-9: the G_0 isomorphism and the clopen rank partition are elementary and correct. Step 10: sober gives T0, and the quasi-compact T0 node gives a closed point in the clopen nonzero-rank locus; no Jacobson hypothesis is needed.
